saints.name: St. Andrew Dung-Lac and Companions
saints.title: Martyrs
saints.shortBlurb: The many martyrs of Vietnam — priests, catechists, and laity — who died for the faith across three centuries of persecution…
biography: This memorial honours a great company of martyrs who died for the Christian faith in Vietnam between the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries, during fierce persecutions under a succession of emperors. Among them were Vietnamese diocesan priests, catechists, and lay men and women, together with European missionaries of the Dominicans and the Paris Foreign Missions.

Their representative, Andrew Dũng-Lạc, was a Vietnamese priest beheaded in 1839. One hundred and seventeen of these martyrs were canonized together in 1988, and through them the whole multitude of Vietnam's witnesses is remembered. They are honoured as patrons of the Church in Vietnam.
saints.knownFor: The witness of the Vietnamese martyrs under persecution.

sources.text: Vatican biography, Canonization of the Martyrs of Vietnam (vatican.va)
